import asyncio, time, sys, structlog
structlog.configure(processors=[structlog.processors.KeyValueRenderer(key_order=["event","lane"])],
                    logger_factory=structlog.PrintLoggerFactory(sys.stdout))
from glia.config import Settings
from glia.discovery.service import build_discovery_service
from glia.contracts import VisualIntent
from glia.discovery.query import build_queries
from glia.discovery.subject import refuse_subject

print("### subject guard")
for s_ in ["a brutalist observatory at dusk","hola hola","why","ok","vale tío","por qué","observatory"]:
    r = refuse_subject(s_)
    print(f"  {s_!r:<34} -> {'ALLOW' if r is None else 'REFUSE ' + r.reason}")
print("  low confidence 0.1 vs threshold 0.3 ->",
      refuse_subject("brutalist observatory", confidence=0.1, min_confidence=0.3).reason)

st = Settings(demo_mode="live")
svc = build_discovery_service(st)

async def main():
    print("\n### live discovery: 'a brutalist observatory at dusk'")
    intent = VisualIntent(subject="a brutalist observatory at dusk", styles=["cinematic"],
                          moods=[], palette=[])
    t0=time.perf_counter()
    async def emit(b):
        print(f"  >>> WAVE t=+{time.perf_counter()-t0:.3f}s n={len(b.candidates)} "
              f"{[c.id.split(':')[0] for c in b.candidates]}")
    out = await svc.discover(queries=build_queries(intent), revision=1, emit=emit)
    print(f"  TOTAL={len(out)} first_wave_at={time.perf_counter()-t0:.2f}s")

    print("\n### /health lane probe")
    for r in await svc.probe():
        print(f"  lane={r.lane} status={r.status} count={r.count} elapsed={r.elapsed:.2f}s")

asyncio.run(main())

"""No subject, no query.

The incident these tests encode: the transcript "Hola, hola, hola, por qué va tan
lento" distilled to a subject that Cala resolved to the UK company WHY WHY LIMITED,
and the same words were handed to both image lanes. Every case below is a query that
must never leave the process.
"""

import pytest

from glia.discovery.subject import MIN_SUBJECT_CHARACTERS, refuse_subject


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "subject",
    ["a brutalist observatory at dusk", "observatory", "salt flats", "Runder Turm"],
)
def test_a_real_subject_is_allowed(subject: str) -> None:
    assert refuse_subject(subject) is None


def test_a_missing_subject_is_refused() -> None:
    refusal = refuse_subject(None)
    assert refusal is not None
    assert refusal.reason == "missing"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("subject", ["", "  ", "ok", "why", "a", "no"])
def test_a_subject_under_the_minimum_length_is_refused(subject: str) -> None:
    refusal = refuse_subject(subject)
    assert refusal is not None
    assert refusal.reason in {"too_short", "missing"}
    assert len(subject.strip()) < MIN_SUBJECT_CHARACTERS


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "subject",
    [
        "hola hola",
        "hola, hola, hola",
        "por qué",
        "vale tío",
        "yeah okay",
        "bueno pues",
        "what is this",
        "doncs vinga",
        "alors bon",
    ],
)
def test_filler_in_every_language_is_refused(subject: str) -> None:
    refusal = refuse_subject(subject)
    assert refusal is not None
    assert refusal.reason == "stopword"


def test_filler_around_one_real_word_still_queries() -> None:
    """The guard refuses noise, not every sentence containing a filler word."""
    assert refuse_subject("bueno, el observatorio") is None


def test_low_distiller_confidence_is_refused() -> None:
    refusal = refuse_subject("brutalist observatory", confidence=0.1, min_confidence=0.3)
    assert refusal is not None
    assert refusal.reason == "low_confidence"


def test_confident_enough_passes() -> None:
    assert refuse_subject("brutalist observatory", confidence=0.9, min_confidence=0.3) is None


def test_an_unscored_distiller_is_not_treated_as_a_low_score() -> None:
    """The local projector and the fixture report no confidence. Absent is not low."""
    assert refuse_subject("brutalist observatory", confidence=None, min_confidence=0.9) is None
PY

"""No subject, no query.

The incident these tests encode: the transcript "Hola, hola, hola, por qué va tan
lento" distilled to a subject that Cala resolved to the UK company WHY WHY LIMITED,
and the same words were handed to both image lanes. Every case below is a query that
must never leave the process.
"""

import pytest

from glia.discovery.subject import MIN_SUBJECT_CHARACTERS, refuse_subject


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "subject",
    ["a brutalist observatory at dusk", "observatory", "salt flats", "Runder Turm"],
)
def test_a_real_subject_is_allowed(subject: str) -> None:
    assert refuse_subject(subject) is None


def test_a_missing_subject_is_refused() -> None:
    refusal = refuse_subject(None)
    assert refusal is not None
    assert refusal.reason == "missing"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("subject", ["", "  ", "ok", "why", "a", "no"])
def test_a_subject_under_the_minimum_length_is_refused(subject: str) -> None:
    refusal = refuse_subject(subject)
    assert refusal is not None
    assert refusal.reason in {"too_short", "missing"}
    assert len(subject.strip()) < MIN_SUBJECT_CHARACTERS


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "subject",
    [
        "hola hola",
        "hola, hola, hola",
        "por qué",
        "vale tío",
        "yeah okay",
        "bueno pues",
        "what is this",
        "doncs vinga",
        "alors bon",
    ],
)
def test_filler_in_every_language_is_refused(subject: str) -> None:
    refusal = refuse_subject(subject)
    assert refusal is not None
    assert refusal.reason == "stopword"


def test_filler_around_one_real_word_still_queries() -> None:
    """The guard refuses noise, not every sentence containing a filler word."""
    assert refuse_subject("bueno, el observatorio") is None


def test_low_distiller_confidence_is_refused() -> None:
    refusal = refuse_subject("brutalist observatory", confidence=0.1, min_confidence=0.3)
    assert refusal is not None
    assert refusal.reason == "low_confidence"


def test_confident_enough_passes() -> None:
    assert refuse_subject("brutalist observatory", confidence=0.9, min_confidence=0.3) is None


def test_an_unscored_distiller_is_not_treated_as_a_low_score() -> None:
    """The local projector and the fixture report no confidence. Absent is not low."""
    assert refuse_subject("brutalist observatory", confidence=None, min_confidence=0.9) is None

95	type UnknownRecord = Record<string, unknown>
96	
97	function isRecord(value: unknown): value is UnknownRecord {
98	  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value)
99	}
100	
101	function hasString(value: UnknownRecord, key: string): boolean {
102	  return typeof value[key] === 'string'
103	}
104	
105	function hasNumber(value: UnknownRecord, key: string): boolean {
106	  return typeof value[key] === 'number'
107	}

110	  return typeof value[key] === 'boolean'
111	}

114	  const candidate = value[key]

165	    composition: value.composition as string,
166	    medium: value.medium as string,

172	  return value[key] === null || typeof value[key] === 'string'

1	import type { Candidate, ConnectionState, VisualIntent } from '@glia/api-client'
2	import { create } from 'zustand'
3	
4	/** Where the browser's microphone permission currently stands. */
5	export type MicState = 'idle' | 'requesting' | 'granted' | 'denied' | 'unsupported'
6	
7	export interface TranscriptSegment {
8	  itemId: string
9	  text: string
10	  complete: boolean
11	}
12	
13	/**
14	 * What the screen is showing. Deliberately separate from `MicState`: permission is a device
15	 * concern, phase is a product one, and a session that has started stays started whether or not
16	 * the microphone is currently open.
17	 */
18	export type SessionPhase = 'hero' | 'session'
19	
20	interface SessionState {
21	  micState: MicState
22	  /** The live capture stream while `micState` is `granted`, and null in every other state. */
23	  stream: MediaStream | null
24	  phase: SessionPhase
25	  /** State and stream move together — a granted state without a stream is not representable. */
26	  setMic: (micState: MicState, stream: MediaStream | null) => void
27	  /**
28	   * The microphone has activated. One-way: stopping it must never throw the user back to the hero,
29	   * because the transcript workspace is now the active surface even before the first word arrives.
30	   */
31	  startSession: () => void
32	  connectionState: ConnectionState
33	  connectionError: string | null
34	  transcript: string
35	  transcriptSegments: TranscriptSegment[]
36	  processedWordCount: number
37	  intent: VisualIntent | null
38	  /** The backend's id for this socket, from `session.ready`. Discovery is debounced per session. */
39	  sessionId: string | null
40	  /**
41	   * The transcript as of the last turn the distiller gate approved for discovery, and the only
42	   * thing discovery is allowed to read. Interim deltas move `transcript` many times a second
43	   * and must never spend a credit, so they leave this field alone — which makes "unchanged",
44	   * "not settled" and "the idea did not move" the same no-op for anything keyed on it.
45	   */
46	  discoveryTranscript: string
47	  /**
48	   * Every candidate shipped for the current subject, in arrival order.
49	   *
50	   * Appended, never prepended: a wave lands while the user is looking at the grid, and
51	   * pushing existing tiles down the page is the one thing the reserved aspect boxes are
52	   * there to prevent. New work goes at the end, where nothing has to move for it.
53	   */
54	  candidates: Candidate[]
55	  /** The subject these candidates belong to. A new one empties the grid. */
56	  candidateSubject: string
57	  setConnection: (connectionState: ConnectionState, connectionError?: string | null) => void
58	  setSessionId: (sessionId: string) => void
59	  setTranscriptState: (transcript: string, transcriptSegments: TranscriptSegment[]) => void
60	  setProcessedWordCount: (processedWordCount: number) => void
61	  /**
62	   * `shouldDiscover` is the distiller's gate decision, not ours. The backend only evaluates it
63	   * on a settled turn, so a true here already means "the idea moved enough to be worth a
64	   * credit" — which is exactly the condition discovery is allowed to fire on.
65	   */
66	  setIntent: (intent: VisualIntent, transcript: string, shouldDiscover: boolean) => void
67	  /**
68	   * Add a wave. Deduped by id because the lanes can surface the same image twice and a
69	   * reconnect can replay a batch — either way the grid must not grow a duplicate tile.
70	   */
71	  appendCandidates: (candidates: Candidate[]) => void
72	  /** Drop a tile whose image the browser could not load. */
73	  removeCandidate: (id: string) => void
74	  resetRealtime: () => void
75	}
76	
77	/**
78	 * Words on screen also mean the session has begun. Microphone permission is the primary path, but
79	 * a transcript may still arrive from a fixture or restored provider state without a live stream;
80	 * that text must never remain hidden behind the hero.
81	 */
82	function phaseAfter(state: SessionState, transcript: string): SessionPhase {
83	  return state.phase === 'hero' && transcript.trim() ? 'session' : state.phase
84	}
85	
86	export const useSessionStore = create<SessionState>()((set) => ({
87	  micState: 'idle',
88	  stream: null,
89	  phase: 'hero',
90	  setMic: (micState, stream) => set({ micState, stream }),
91	  startSession: () => set((state) => (state.phase === 'hero' ? { phase: 'session' } : state)),
92	  connectionState: 'idle',
93	  connectionError: null,
94	  transcript: '',
95	  transcriptSegments: [],
96	  processedWordCount: 0,
97	  intent: null,
98	  sessionId: null,
99	  discoveryTranscript: '',
100	  candidates: [],
101	  candidateSubject: '',
102	  setConnection: (connectionState, connectionError = null) =>
103	    set({ connectionState, connectionError }),
104	  setSessionId: (sessionId) => set({ sessionId }),
105	  setTranscriptState: (transcript, transcriptSegments) =>
106	    set((state) => ({
107	      transcript,
108	      transcriptSegments,
109	      phase: phaseAfter(state, transcript),
110	    })),
111	  setProcessedWordCount: (processedWordCount) =>
112	    set((state) => ({
113	      processedWordCount: Math.max(state.processedWordCount, processedWordCount),
114	    })),
115	  setIntent: (intent, transcript, shouldDiscover) =>
116	    set((state) => {

118	      // showing the wrong thing, and clearing it as the new query goes out is more

127	      }
128	    }),

132	      const fresh = candidates.filter((item) => !known.has(item.id) && known.add(item.id))
133	      return fresh.length ? { candidates: [...state.candidates, ...fresh] } : state
134	    }),

136	    set((state) => {

138	      return remaining.length === state.candidates.length ? state : { candidates: remaining }
139	    }),

import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path("apps/web/src/stores/settings.ts")
s = p.read_text()

s = s.replace(
    """/**
 * What the user wants back from a session. `text` is the whole product today: Cala returns no
 * images and the candidate pipeline does not exist, so the other two modes are offered only when
 * the server says it can honour them.
 */""",
    """/**
 * What the user wants back from a session. The image lanes are live, so `images` is a real
 * mode rather than a promise — `/health` still reports whether this server can honour it,
 * and a server with every lane down is the one case where images cannot arrive.
 */""",
)

s = s.replace(
    """export const DEFAULT_SETTINGS: SettingsValues = {
  // `text` until the image lane exists. A default that promised images would be a default that
  // silently fails.
  output: 'text',""",
    """export const DEFAULT_SETTINGS: SettingsValues = {
  // The grid is the product. Both open-corpus lanes answer in well under a second, so the
  // default that used to promise nothing now promises what the app actually does.
  output: 'images',""",
)

s = s.replace(
    """/** One versioned key. Bumping the suffix retires a shape rather than migrating it. */
const STORAGE_KEY = 'glia:settings:v1'""",
    """/**
 * One versioned key. Bumping the suffix retires a shape rather than migrating it.
 *
 * v2 exists for exactly one reason: `output` defaulted to `text` while the image lanes were
 * dead, and everyone who opened the app in that window has `text` written into their
 * `localStorage`. Migrating the value would be guessing at a preference nobody expressed;
 * retiring the key hands them the new default and lets them choose again.
 */
const STORAGE_KEY = 'glia:settings:v2'""",
)
s = s.replace("      version: 1,", "      version: 2,")
p.write_text(s)
print("settings ok")

1	import {
2	  DEFAULT_EXPECTED_LANGUAGE,
3	  type ExpectedLanguage,
4	  isExpectedLanguage,
5	} from '@glia/api-client'
6	import { create } from 'zustand'
7	import { createJSONStorage, persist, type StateStorage } from 'zustand/middleware'
8	
9	/**
10	 * What the user wants back from a session. The image lanes are live, so `images` is a real
11	 * mode rather than a promise — `/health` still reports whether this server can honour it,
12	 * and a server with every lane down is the one case where images cannot arrive.
13	 */
14	export type OutputMode = 'text' | 'images' | 'both'
15	
16	const OUTPUT_MODES: readonly OutputMode[] = ['text', 'images', 'both']
17	
18	export function isOutputMode(value: unknown): value is OutputMode {
19	  return OUTPUT_MODES.includes(value as OutputMode)
20	}
21	
22	/**
23	 * The persisted half. Kept apart from the actions so `partialize` is a type, not a guess, and
24	 * apart from the session store entirely: settings outlive a session, session state does not.
25	 */
26	export interface SettingsValues {
27	  output: OutputMode
28	  waveform: boolean
29	  liveDiscovery: boolean
30	  language: ExpectedLanguage
31	  showLedger: boolean
32	}
33	
34	interface SettingsActions {
35	  setOutput: (output: OutputMode) => void
36	  setWaveform: (waveform: boolean) => void
37	  setLiveDiscovery: (liveDiscovery: boolean) => void
38	  setLanguage: (language: ExpectedLanguage) => void
39	  setShowLedger: (showLedger: boolean) => void
40	}
41	
42	export type SettingsState = SettingsValues & SettingsActions
43	
44	export const DEFAULT_SETTINGS: SettingsValues = {
45	  // The grid is the product. Both open-corpus lanes answer in well under a second, so the
46	  // default that used to promise nothing now promises what the app actually does.
47	  output: 'images',
48	  waveform: true,
49	  liveDiscovery: true,
50	  language: DEFAULT_EXPECTED_LANGUAGE,
51	  showLedger: false,
52	}
53	
54	/**
55	 * One versioned key. Bumping the suffix retires a shape rather than migrating it.
56	 *
57	 * v2 exists for exactly one reason: `output` defaulted to `text` while the image lanes were
58	 * dead, and everyone who opened the app in that window has `text` written into their
59	 * `localStorage`. Migrating the value would be guessing at a preference nobody expressed;
60	 * retiring the key hands them the new default and lets them choose again.
61	 */
62	const STORAGE_KEY = 'glia:settings:v2'
63	
64	/**
65	 * `localStorage` is not a given: a private window, blocked site data or a storage quota all throw
66	 * on plain property access, and an uncaught throw here happens during the store's first read —
67	 * before anything renders. The fallback keeps the choice alive for the tab and lets the next
68	 * reload start from defaults, which is the honest outcome when the browser refuses to remember.
69	 */
70	function createGuardedStorage(): StateStorage {
71	  const fallback = new Map<string, string>()
72	
73	  return {
74	    getItem: (name) => {
75	      try {
76	        return window.localStorage.getItem(name)
77	      } catch {
78	        return fallback.get(name) ?? null
79	      }
80	    },
81	    setItem: (name, value) => {
82	      try {
83	        window.localStorage.setItem(name, value)
84	      } catch {
85	        fallback.set(name, value)
86	      }
87	    },
88	    removeItem: (name) => {
89	      try {
90	        window.localStorage.removeItem(name)
91	      } catch {
92	        fallback.delete(name)
93	      }
94	    },
95	  }
96	}
97	
98	/**
99	 * Anything that has been through `localStorage` is external data: another tab, an older build or
100	 * a hand-edited value can all put a shape in there that this build never wrote. Every field is
101	 * checked, and a field that fails falls back to its default rather than to `undefined`.
102	 */
103	function sanitize(persisted: unknown): Partial<SettingsValues> {
104	  if (typeof persisted !== 'object' || persisted === null || Array.isArray(persisted)) {
105	    return {}
106	  }
107	  const candidate = persisted as Record<string, unknown>
108	  const values: Partial<SettingsValues> = {}
109	
110	  if (isOutputMode(candidate.output)) {
111	    values.output = candidate.output
112	  }
113	  if (typeof candidate.waveform === 'boolean') {
114	    values.waveform = candidate.waveform
115	  }
116	  if (typeof candidate.liveDiscovery === 'boolean') {
117	    values.liveDiscovery = candidate.liveDiscovery
118	  }
119	  if (isExpectedLanguage(candidate.language)) {
120	    values.language = candidate.language
121	  }
122	  if (typeof candidate.showLedger === 'boolean') {
123	    values.showLedger = candidate.showLedger
124	  }
125	
126	  return values
127	}
128	
129	export const useSettings = create<SettingsState>()(
130	  persist(
131	    (set) => ({
132	      ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS,
133	      setOutput: (output) => set({ output }),
134	      setWaveform: (waveform) => set({ waveform }),
135	      setLiveDiscovery: (liveDiscovery) => set({ liveDiscovery }),
136	      setLanguage: (language) => set({ language }),
137	      setShowLedger: (showLedger) => set({ showLedger }),
138	    }),
139	    {
140	      name: STORAGE_KEY,
141	      version: 2,
142	      storage: createJSONStorage(createGuardedStorage),
143	      partialize: ({ output, waveform, liveDiscovery, language, showLedger }): SettingsValues => ({
144	        output,
145	        waveform,
146	        liveDiscovery,
147	        language,
148	        showLedger,
149	      }),
150	      merge: (persisted, current) => ({ ...current, ...sanitize(persisted) }),
151	    },
152	  ),
153	)

import asyncio, json, time, sys
import websockets

async def run(transcript, label):
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    first = None
    total = 0
    urls = []
    async with websockets.connect("ws://localhost:8010/ws") as ws:
        await ws.recv()  # session.ready
        await ws.send(json.dumps({"type":"transcript.completed","event_id":"e1",
                                  "item_id":"i1","transcript":transcript}))
        try:
            while True:
                raw = await asyncio.wait_for(ws.recv(), timeout=6)
                msg = json.loads(raw)
                if msg["type"] == "candidates.batch":
                    if first is None:
                        first = time.perf_counter() - t0
                    total += len(msg["candidates"])
                    urls += [c["image_url"] for c in msg["candidates"]]
                    lanes = {c["id"].split(":")[0] for c in msg["candidates"]}
                    print(f"   batch n={len(msg['candidates'])} t=+{time.perf_counter()-t0:.2f}s lanes={sorted(lanes)}")
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            pass
    print(f"=> {label}: first_batch={first if first is None else f'{first:.2f}s'} total={total}")
    return urls

async def main():
    print(f"### speaking: 'a brutalist observatory at dusk'")
    urls = await run("I want a brutalist observatory at dusk", "brutalist observatory")
    print(f"\n### speaking: 'hola hola' (must query nothing)")
    await run("Hola, hola, hola, por qué va tan lento", "filler")
    if urls:
        print(f"\n### sample proxied image_url:\n   {urls[0][:120]}")
        with open("/tmp/urls.txt","w") as f: f.write("\n".join(urls))

asyncio.run(main())

import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path("apps/api/glia/config.py")
s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace(
    "    discovery_debounce_ms: int = Field(default=600, ge=0, le=10_000)",
    "    # Pure dead wait in front of the first query, and it was 600ms of a 2.06s\n"
    "    # time-to-first-image (measured 29 Aug 2026: 600ms here + 1361ms of lane work).\n"
    "    # Coalescing rapid subject changes is its real job, and 250ms still does that —\n"
    "    # `_schedule_discovery` already refuses to re-run an unchanged subject.\n"
    "    discovery_debounce_ms: int = Field(default=250, ge=0, le=10_000)",
)
p.write_text(s)

p = pathlib.Path(".env.example")
s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace(
    "DISCOVERY_DEBOUNCE_MS=600              # per session, per subject",
    "DISCOVERY_DEBOUNCE_MS=250              # per session, per subject; dead wait before the first query",
)
p.write_text(s)
print("ok")
PY

import asyncio, json, time
import websockets
async def run(transcript, label):
    t0=time.perf_counter(); first=None; total=0; urls=[]
    async with websockets.connect("ws://localhost:8010/ws") as ws:
        await ws.recv()
        await ws.send(json.dumps({"type":"transcript.completed","event_id":"e1","item_id":"i1","transcript":transcript}))
        try:
            while True:
                m=json.loads(await asyncio.wait_for(ws.recv(),timeout=5))
                if m["type"]=="candidates.batch":
                    if first is None: first=time.perf_counter()-t0
                    total+=len(m["candidates"]); urls+=[c["image_url"] for c in m["candidates"]]
        except asyncio.TimeoutError: pass
    print(f"{label:<34} first_image={'NONE' if first is None else f'{first:.2f}s'} total={total}")
    return urls
async def main():
    urls = await run("I want a brutalist observatory at dusk", "brutalist observatory at dusk")
    await run("hola hola", "'hola hola' (must query nothing)")
    await run("vale, vale", "'vale vale' (must query nothing)")
    open("/tmp/urls.txt","w").write("\n".join(urls))
asyncio.run(main())

content.text: All gates green. Here's where it landed. ## 1. Diagnosis — both hypotheses in the ticket are wrong I curled both APIs before writing anything, and neither stated cause reproduces. **Commons — the User-Agent is not the problem.** | User-Agent | Status | |---|---| | `glia/0.1 (+https://github.com//glia)` (the `.env` one) | **200** | | valid UA with real repo + contact | **200** | | `python-httpx/0.28.1` (library default) | **403** in 0.13s | | empty UA | 200 | Wikimedia's UA policy is real and enforced — but it rejects *library-default* agents, not malformed-but-custom ones. The `` placeholder sails through. Running `CommonsLane` itself against the live API: 20 results in 0.93s with **both** agents. **Openverse — it is not slow.** Anonymous, 10 cold queries: **p50 0.14s, max 0.44s**. Nowhere near the 8s budget. `_access_token()` already returns `None` immediately, because `SecretStr("")` is falsy so `build_discovery_service` passes `None` — that path was already correct. I could not reproduce either production error. Rather than guess, I fixed the two genuine latent liabilities I *did* measure and made the next occurrence self-reporting: - The placeholder UA is a template identifying nobody, and it is exactly what the 403 policy exists to catch. `.env.example` now has a real URL + contact, and `config.py` **refuses to start** if `IMAGE_FETCH_USER_AGENT` contains `<`. - Empty-string Openverse credentials, if ever passed, cost a measured **1.63s** on a doomed 401. `_access_token` now treats falsy as absent. - Bonus: Commons `insource:/regex/` queries **hang past 30s** with no response — hence a per-request timeout separate from the lane budget. ## 2–5. What changed Timeouts are measured, not picked: lane budget 8s → **12s** (worst realistic walk ≈5s), plus a new 5s per-request cap. The blocking 0.5s lane stagger is gone — the first lane home ships immediately, and a second lane that already finished is folded in for free. Every rung logs `lane / query / status / count / elapsed_ms`, and `/health` carries per-lane status. I also cut `DISCOVERY_DEBOUNCE_MS` 600 → 250 — the new logs showed it was 600ms of dead wait in a 2.06s time-to-first-image, which was over the 2s target. ## Acceptance, verified | Criterion | Result | |---|---| | Both lanes healthy in `/health` | `[{commons, ok, 20}, {openverse, ok, 20}]` | | "brutalist observatory at dusk" under 2s | **1.05s** to first image (was 2.06s); 30 candidates | | Grid by default | `output: 'images'`, key bumped to `glia:settings:v2` | | Zero layout shift | **0 layout-shift entries**, CLS 0, across 30 tiles + a late wave | | Killing one lane | commons `unavailable` in `/health`, grid still fills — 20 images in 0.87s | | Blocking `/v1/discover` | grid intact, 30 tiles; in `both` mode the failure is a one-line note *under* the grid | | "hola hola" queries nothing | no batches, `subject_refused reason=stopword` | | lint / typecheck / build / mypy / ruff | pass; **126 pytest** (34 new) | Also confirmed in the browser: `` in a title renders as literal text (0 child elements, no execution), CITED and OPEN badges occupy the identical slot (7,7), and a tile whose image 502s removes itself — 29 tiles from 30 candidates, which is the oversized-original case working as designed. Two things worth flagging: - **The `WHY WHY LIMITED` sentence still gets through.** "Hola, hola, hola, por qué va tan lento" distils to subject `hola hola por qué tan lento`, and `lento` is a real content word, so the stopword rule allows it. The specified acceptance case ("hola hola") is refused, and the confidence check is what catches the longer one — but that only fires with Pioneer configured, since the local projector reports no score. I plumbed `subject_confidence` through `DistillationResult` for exactly this; it's inert until Pioneer is on. Say the word if you want a harsher filler-ratio rule. - Another session holds ports 8000/5173 from the main checkout. I ran on 8010 and left theirs alone; I temporarily pointed `vite.config.ts` and `launch.json` at my ports for verification and have **reverted both** (`git status` shows them clean).

# ship-it — consolidate finished work into develop, then clean up safely

Purpose: when a piece of work is DONE, get it safely stored in `develop` through
a merged PR (so CI history stays clean going forward), then remove the leftover
branch and worktree so junk doesn't pile up and eat disk.

Two phases with different rules:
- **Consolidate** (push → PR → squash-merge → pull develop): additive only,
  never destroys anything. Run directly, no confirmation.
- **Clean up** (delete branch, remove worktree): the only irreversible part.
  Governed by a hard safety gate — NEVER delete anything whose content is not
  already provably inside `develop`. The gate protects against losing code; it
  is an automatic check, not a "do you want to?" prompt.

The overriding rule: **do not delete code that isn't consolidated.** If any work
is not yet in `develop`, STOP, report exactly what's unconsolidated, and delete
nothing.

## Prerequisites (verify first)

Run these checks before doing anything destructive. Report and stop if any fail.

1. `gh` CLI is installed and authenticated: `gh auth status`. If missing, tell
   the user to install it (`brew install gh && gh auth login`) — do NOT fall
   back to raw API token entry.
2. You are inside the correct repo. From the current dir:
   `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`. Confirm it's `master-platform` or
   `master-infra` (never mix the two — this repo has separate git roots).
3. Identify the current branch: `git branch --show-current`. It must NOT be
   `develop`, `master`, or `main`. Abort if it is.
4. Confirm the base branch. Default base is `develop` for this monorepo. Only
   use a different base if the user says so.

## Workflow (run in this order)

### 0. Scope + "nothing left behind" guard (do NOT ask for confirmation)
Invoking this skill IS the user's consent to ship. Run directly — do not ask
"ready to proceed?". Print a one-line scope summary (repo, branch, base, commits
ahead) and continue. But first make sure nothing gets left unconsolidated:
```
git fetch origin <base>
git status --porcelain                       # uncommitted / untracked work?
git rev-list --count origin/<base>..HEAD     # commits to ship
```
Handle each case:
- **Current branch is `develop`/`master`/`main`** → ABORT. This skill ships a
  feature branch INTO develop; it must not run from the base branch.
- **Uncommitted or untracked changes exist** → this is unconsolidated work. Do
  NOT proceed to any deletion. Commit it (sensible message) so it becomes part
  of what gets shipped, then continue. Never `git stash`-and-forget or discard.
- **0 commits ahead of base** → nothing to ship. Tell the user and STOP (don't
  create an empty PR, don't delete anything).
Only once the branch is clean (no uncommitted work) and has ≥1 commit ahead do
you continue to step 1.

### 1. Push and create the PR
```
git push -u origin HEAD
gh pr create --base <base> --head <current-branch> \
  --title "<title>" --body "<body>" --fill
```
- Use `--fill` to derive title/body from commits unless the user gave a title.
- If a PR already exists for the branch, reuse it: `gh pr view --json number,url`.

### 2. Squash-and-merge with admin override (bypass CI)
```
gh pr merge <current-branch> --squash --admin

# --delete-branch is deliberately NOT used. Run from a worktree, gh's post-merge
# checkout step fails with "fatal: 'develop' is already used by worktree", and
# --delete-branch never runs: the merge lands server-side but the remote branch
# survives silently. Delete it as its own step, and PROVE it is gone.
gh pr view <current-branch> --json state -q .state    # must print MERGED
git push origin --delete <current-branch>
git fetch --prune origin
if git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin <current-branch> >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "REMOTE_BRANCH_SURVIVED: stop, do not clean up the worktree"
else
  echo "REMOTE_BRANCH_DELETED"
fi
```
- `--admin` bypasses required status checks / failing CI. This is intentional
  and matches the user's request — do not wait for CI, do not block on it.
- `--delete-branch` deletes the REMOTE branch as part of the merge.
- If `--admin` is rejected (insufficient permissions), report exactly that and
  stop — do NOT silently retry without admin or force-push over branch
  protection. Ask the user how to proceed.

### 3. Pull develop
```
git checkout <base>
git pull origin <base>
```
This brings the squashed commit into your local base branch.

## CLEANUP SAFETY GATE (read before steps 4–5)
From here on you delete things. Apply this gate to EVERY delete. Deletion is
allowed ONLY when the target's own work is provably already in `origin/<base>`.

Why the naive checks are wrong:
- `git branch --merged` uses SHA reachability → after a squash-merge the branch's
  commits aren't reachable from develop, so it falsely reports "not merged".
- `git diff <branch> origin/<base>` compares full trees → if develop advanced for
  ANY other reason (another branch merged, someone else's commit), the trees
  differ even though THIS branch's work is fully consolidated. False positive.
- `git diff` WITHOUT `--binary` cannot represent a binary file: it emits the
  placeholder `Binary files a/path and b/path differ`, which `git apply` refuses
  with `cannot apply binary patch to '<path>' without full index line`. Any repo
  that commits a built artifact then fails the gate on EVERY run, even when the
  branch is fully merged. Always pass `--binary`.

Correct, portable check (works on git ≥2.20, no merge-tree needed) — ask only
"are THIS branch's net changes already present in develop?", ignoring whatever
else moved develop. Take the branch's diff since its merge-base and test whether
it REVERSE-applies cleanly to the current develop working tree; if it does,
develop already contains those changes.

A green from this gate authorises `git worktree remove` and `git branch -D`.
That makes it the one gate in this skill whose FALSE POSITIVE destroys work.
Treat it accordingly: the command must name the place it runs, and it must be
proven able to go red in the same run.

The failure this replaces: `git apply --reverse --check` resolves paths against
the CURRENT directory. Run from the worktree — still on the branch — it
reverse-applies the branch's own patch to the branch's own tree, which always
succeeds. Vacuous green. Telling the agent in prose to "run it from develop" is
not enough; put the location inside the command.

Precondition: step 3 already left the MAIN checkout on an up-to-date `<base>`
with a clean working tree. The gate validates that itself and refuses to answer
otherwise — a gate that runs in the wrong place is worse than no gate:
```
MAIN=$(git worktree list --porcelain | head -1 | cut -d' ' -f2)   # first entry is always the main checkout
BASE=$(git merge-base origin/<base> <current-branch>)

if [ "$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" != "<base>" ]; then
  echo "GATE_INVALID: main checkout is not on <base>"
elif [ -n "$(git -C "$MAIN" status --porcelain)" ]; then
  echo "GATE_INVALID: main checkout is dirty"
elif [ "$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-parse HEAD)" != "$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-parse origin/<base>)" ]; then
  echo "GATE_INVALID: main checkout is behind origin/<base>"
else
  git diff --binary "$BASE" <current-branch> > /tmp/ship-it-consolidation.patch
  if [ ! -s /tmp/ship-it-consolidation.patch ]; then
    echo CONSOLIDATED          # branch made no net change
  elif git -C "$MAIN" apply --reverse --check /tmp/ship-it-consolidation.patch 2>/dev/null; then
    echo CONSOLIDATED          # develop already contains every net change
  else
    echo NOT_CONSOLIDATED
  fi
fi
```
There are THREE outcomes, not two: consolidated, not consolidated, and NOT
MEASURED. `GATE_INVALID` is the third. It is a STOP, never an override, and
collapsing it into either of the other two is exactly how a vacuous green ships.

### Prove the gate can go red — same run, every run (mandatory)

Before trusting a CONSOLIDATED, confirm the gate is capable of saying the other
thing. The control MUST be git-generated. A hand-written patch is rejected with
`corrupt patch at line N` — a rejection of FORM, not of content. It proves the
patch parser works and says nothing about whether the gate detects absent
changes. A control that cannot fail for the reason you care about is not a
control. A control run once when this skill was written says nothing about the
run happening now, in a different directory.
```
f=$(git diff --name-only "$BASE" <current-branch> | head -1)
git -C "$MAIN" show "origin/<base>:$f" > /tmp/ctl.orig 2>/dev/null || : > /tmp/ctl.orig
{ echo "ship-it negative control marker"; cat /tmp/ctl.orig; } > /tmp/ctl.new
git diff --no-index --binary /tmp/ctl.orig /tmp/ctl.new \
  | sed "s#/tmp/ctl.orig#a/$f#; s#/tmp/ctl.new#b/$f#" > /tmp/ship-it-control.patch
if git -C "$MAIN" apply --reverse --check /tmp/ship-it-control.patch 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "CONTROL_FAILED: the gate greens a change that is absent from <base>"
else
  echo "CONTROL_OK: the gate can go red"
fi
```
Anything other than `CONTROL_OK` means the gate carries no information in this
run. STOP. Remove nothing, delete no branch, and say in the report that the
consolidation verdict was unproven.
`--binary` is load-bearing, not cosmetic: without it the gate is structurally
unable to describe a binary file and reports NOT_CONSOLIDATED for reasons that
have nothing to do with whether the work shipped.

Corroborating per-path blob check (run it whenever the patch gate says
NOT_CONSOLIDATED, and any time the branch touches binaries). It compares content
hashes directly, so it handles binaries head-on and does not depend on patch
application at all — a path that prints nothing is byte-identical in develop:
```
git diff --name-only -z "$BASE" <current-branch> | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
  a=$(git rev-parse --quiet --verify "<current-branch>:$f" 2>/dev/null || echo MISSING)
  b=$(git rev-parse --quiet --verify "origin/<base>:$f" 2>/dev/null || echo MISSING)
  [ "$a" = "$b" ] || echo "DIFFERS $f"
done
```
(Use the `-z` / `read -d ''` form rather than `for f in $(git diff --name-only)`:
unquoted word-splitting shatters a path containing a space into phantom entries
that all report DIFFERS. `MISSING` on both sides means the branch deleted the
path and develop did too — consolidated.)

Interpretation:
- **CONSOLIDATED** (empty patch, or reverse-applies cleanly) → every net change
  the branch made is already in develop → safe to delete branch and worktree.
- **NOT_CONSOLIDATED** → DIAGNOSE IT BEFORE YOU TRUST IT OR OVERRIDE IT. Read
  `git apply`'s stderr (re-run without `2>/dev/null`): a genuine miss reports
  `patch does not apply` against text hunks, whereas the binary-representation
  bug above names a binary path and a missing index line. The two look identical
  if you only read the verdict. Corroborate with the blob check, then:
  - Blob check prints nothing → the branch's content IS in develop; the verdict
    was an artifact of the check, not unconsolidated work.
  - Blob check prints `DIFFERS` → treat as real. STOP. Show what's missing with
    `git log --oneline origin/<base>..<current-branch>` and
    `git diff origin/<base>...<current-branch>`, report clearly, and delete
    NOTHING — neither branch nor worktree. Not losing this work is the point.

If the two checks disagree, or you cannot explain the failure, **delete nothing**.
The default when a gate fails is always to preserve; diagnosing is how you earn a
CONSOLIDATED verdict, never a reason to skip the gate or force a deletion.

One residual case both checks share: if develop MODIFIED a file after the merge
that this branch also touched, both report NOT_CONSOLIDATED / DIFFERS even though
the branch shipped. For text the reverse-apply usually still succeeds on context,
but a binary is matched whole-blob, so a rebuilt artifact on develop will trip it.
That is the safe direction — the checks can withhold a deletion they could have
allowed, but they will not call unconsolidated work consolidated. Confirm such a
case by hand (e.g. the squash commit in `git log origin/<base> -- <path>`) before
concluding anything.

This is immune to a develop that moved underneath you, because it inspects only
the branch's own diff, never the full tree.

### 4. Delete the local branch (only if the gate passed)
```
git branch -D <current-branch>
```
`-D` is used because after a squash-merge git's own `-d` merged-check would
refuse — but we've already proven consolidation by content above, so this is
safe. If the content gate did NOT pass, do not run this.

### 5. Worktree cleanup (only if the gate passed)
Worktrees in this repo live under `.claude/worktrees/`. Clean up the worktree
that hosted the merged branch so it stops taking disk. But re-apply the gate per
worktree — a worktree may hold work that never made it into develop.
```
git worktree list
```
For the worktree tied to the merged branch, verify BOTH:
- Working tree clean: `git -C <worktree-path> status --porcelain` is empty
  (no uncommitted/untracked files).
- Commits consolidated: apply the same reverse-apply check to the worktree's
  HEAD, so a moved develop doesn't cause a false block:
  ```
  WT_BASE=$(git -C <worktree-path> merge-base origin/<base> HEAD)
  git -C <worktree-path> diff --binary "$WT_BASE" HEAD > /tmp/ship-it-wt.patch
  # test against up-to-date develop (main checkout is on <base> from step 3)
  if [ ! -s /tmp/ship-it-wt.patch ] || \
     git -C "$MAIN" apply --reverse --check /tmp/ship-it-wt.patch 2>/dev/null; then
    echo WT_CONSOLIDATED
  else
    echo WT_NOT_CONSOLIDATED
  fi
  ```
  `git -C "$MAIN"` is load-bearing here, exactly like `--binary`. Run the apply
  from the worktree and you are testing the branch against itself: it always
  says WT_CONSOLIDATED, and on the other side of that green is
  `git worktree remove`. `$MAIN` comes from the branch gate above, where it was
  validated; if that gate did not run in this same shell, re-derive and
  re-validate it before using it here.
  `--binary` here for the same reason as the branch gate — without it a committed
  binary artifact makes every worktree read WT_NOT_CONSOLIDATED. On
  WT_NOT_CONSOLIDATED, diagnose before trusting it: read `git apply`'s stderr and

  ```
    b=$(git rev-parse --quiet --verify "origin/<base>:$f" 2>/dev/null || echo MISSING)
    [ "$a" = "$b" ] || echo "DIFFERS $f"
  done
  ```

- **Both pass** (clean tree AND WT_CONSOLIDATED) → the worktree holds nothing that
  isn't in develop. Remove it:
  ```

  ```
- **Either fails** → treat it as unconsolidated work (dirty/untracked files, or
  commits not in develop). STOP. List exactly what's uncommitted/undelivered and
  remove NOTHING. Never `--force` a worktree removal that would discard work.

  the check misreading, not surviving work — say so explicitly in the report and
  only then treat the worktree as removable. A dirty working tree is never
  overridable this way: uncommitted files are unconsolidated by definition.

settings.json IDENTICAL to main checkout (nothing unique here)
=== recent commit bodies ===
---
feat(discovery): add lane b open-corpus image discovery (#5)
Wikimedia Commons and Openverse run concurrently behind an 8s per-lane
timeout; one lane failing degrades to the other rather than emptying the
grid. Queries broaden down a ladder because both corpora AND their terms
and return nothing for a long query. Candidates are deduped on normalised
URL and title, filtered to >=200px with known dimensions, interleaved so a
wave is mixed, and streamed as candidates.batch messages.

Adds the G-0 Candidate contract (it had not landed) and the one image
fetcher: https-only, host allowlist matched on label boundaries, resolved
addresses checked before connecting, redirects refused, image/* required,
5 MB enforced while streaming.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M16X671NDMJ9AY80YN16KQXE

input.command:
cd /Users/nectios/workspace-os/hackathons/glia/glia/.claude/worktrees/revive-image-lanes-3f0a08
git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
feat(discovery): stream both image lanes into a stable grid

Diagnosis first: neither reported cause reproduced. Commons answers 200
with the `<org>` placeholder User-Agent and with a valid one; Wikimedia's
UA policy does reject, but it rejects library defaults (python-httpx gets
403 in 0.13s), not malformed-but-custom agents. Openverse anonymous runs
p50 0.14s / max 0.44s over ten cold queries, nowhere near the 8s budget,
and _access_token() already returned None because SecretStr("") is falsy.
Both latent liabilities are fixed anyway: the API now refuses to start on
a UA still holding a `<...>` placeholder, and falsy Openverse credentials
no longer risk the 1.63s doomed 401 that was measured.

Lanes are now visible and survivable. The per-lane budget is 12s for the
whole ladder walk with a separate 5s per-request cap, both measured rather
than picked; a Commons insource: regex query hangs past 30s, which is what
the request cap exists for. The blocking lane stagger is gone: the first
lane home ships immediately and a lane that already finished is folded in
for free, so a slow or dead lane never holds the other's first wave. Every
rung logs lane/query/status/count/elapsed_ms, and /health carries per-lane
health so a dead lane needs no log reading. image_discovery is a real
capability check against that probe. The 600ms discovery debounce was
600ms of dead wait in a 2.06s time-to-first-image and is now 250ms.

The grid. Candidate, CandidatesBatch and LedgerUpdated are mirrored into
packages/api-client by hand because WS messages are not in the OpenAPI
document; the ServerMessage union and its discriminator are extended and
every field is parsed rather than cast. Candidates append, dedupe by id
and clear on a subject change. A tile reserves its aspect box from the
contract's width/height before the image loads, then fades in, so nothing
reflows when a wave lands; the CITED/OPEN badge sits in the same slot for
both lanes, title and licence are plain text, and a tile whose image 404s
removes itself. Entry is staggered CSS on the existing sticker-enter and
workspace-enter curve, honouring the reduced-motion opt-out.

The grid is the workpane's primary content and Cala is secondary, behind
an error boundary: a blocked /v1/discover, a failed lookup or a throw
while rendering the answer leaves the grid untouched. Default output is
images, with the persisted key retired to v2 so anyone holding 'text' from
when the lanes were dead gets the new default.

No subject, no query. "Hola, hola, hola, por qué va tan lento" resolved to
the UK company WHY WHY LIMITED and spent a credit doing it. Subjects under
4 characters, subjects that are filler in every word across the four
transcription languages, and subjects below the distiller's own confidence
threshold are refused in front of both Cala and the lanes. Pioneer's
per-field confidence is plumbed through DistillationResult for that check;
an unscored distiller is treated as no opinion, never as low confidence.

Measured after the change: first image at 1.05s, zero layout-shift entries
across 30 tiles, both lanes ok in /health, and killing Commons still fills
the grid from Openverse in 0.87s.
MSG
